The Sixth Sense.premise: A psychologist helps a troubled boy who reports encounters with ghosts.
The Sixth Sense.plot: Malcolm treats Cole after being shot by a former patient. Cole learns to help spirits, including a girl whose mother poisoned her, and gains his mother’s trust. Malcolm eventually understands that the shooting killed him and that he too is a ghost. He says farewell to his sleeping wife and departs.

Fight Club.premise: An unhappy office worker and Tyler Durden establish an underground fighting club.
Fight Club.plot: The narrator meets Marla through support groups and moves in with Tyler after his apartment explodes. Their club develops into violent Project Mayhem; Bob dies during a mission. The narrator discovers Tyler is another identity of himself. He shoots himself to suppress Tyler, but the planned destruction of financial buildings proceeds while he watches with Marla.

Shutter Island (film).premise: Two apparent marshals investigate a missing patient at an isolated psychiatric hospital.
Shutter Island (film).plot: Teddy suspects a conspiracy while searching the hospital and lighthouse. Doctors explain he is actually patient Andrew Laeddis, who killed his wife after she drowned their children. Chuck is his psychiatrist, and the investigation was therapeutic roleplay. After briefly acknowledging reality, Andrew appears to relapse and is led away for a lobotomy; his final question leaves his intention ambiguous.

Arrival (film).premise: Linguist Louise Banks works with scientist Ian Donnelly to communicate with visiting extraterrestrials.
Arrival (film).plot: International mistrust threatens war, and soldiers bomb a vessel. The aliens’ language allows non-linear experience of time. Louise’s apparent memories of Hannah are visions of her future daughter. Information from a future encounter lets Louise persuade General Shang to halt an attack. She chooses a family with Ian despite foreseeing Hannah’s fatal illness and their separation.

Get Out.premise: Black photographer Chris visits the family of his white girlfriend Rose.
Get Out.plot: Hypnosis immobilizes Chris, and the household’s behavior grows alarming. He discovers Rose helps lure Black victims into a scheme transplanting white people’s brains into their bodies. Chris blocks the hypnotic trigger using chair stuffing and fights his way out. A camera flash lets Walter briefly regain control; Walter shoots Rose and himself. Chris’s friend Rod arrives and rescues him.

Knives Out.premise: Detective Benoit Blanc investigates wealthy novelist Harlan Thrombey’s death among his family and staff.
Knives Out.plot: Nurse Marta thinks she mixed Harlan’s medicine, and Harlan kills himself to protect her. She inherits the estate. Blanc uncovers Ransom’s attempted medication sabotage, but Marta actually administered the right drug. Ransom kills housekeeper Fran to conceal evidence. Marta tricks him into a confession; his attempted stabbing uses a prop knife. He is arrested, and Marta keeps the inheritance.

Parasite.premise: An impoverished family obtains jobs with a wealthy household while concealing their relationship.
Parasite.plot: The Kims replace the Parks’ employees through deception. Former housekeeper Moon-gwang reveals that her husband Geun-sae secretly occupies a bunker beneath the house. A fight and a flood undermine the Kims’ plan. At a garden party Geun-sae attacks Ki-woo and kills Ki-jung; Chung-sook kills him. Ki-taek kills Mr Park and hides in the bunker. Ki-woo dreams of buying the house to release his father.

Seven.premise: Detectives Somerset and Mills investigate killings organized around the seven deadly sins.
Seven.plot: The detectives identify John Doe through his reading habits after investigating several gruesome murders. Doe surrenders and leads them into the countryside for the final two sins. A package contains the head of Mills’s wife Tracy, who was pregnant. Doe claims envy of Mills’s life. Mills kills Doe in rage, completing the killer’s intended pattern through wrath.

The Usual Suspects.premise: A survivor recounts criminal associates’ involvement in a deadly ship incident during police questioning.
The Usual Suspects.plot: Verbal describes five suspects meeting after a police lineup and committing robberies before being coerced by a lawyer acting for Keyser Söze. A ship raid kills the others and a witness who could identify Söze. After releasing Verbal, Kujan notices his account was assembled from objects in the office. Verbal’s disability disappears as he leaves, and a facial sketch identifies him as Söze.

Oldboy (2003 film).premise: A man released after fifteen years of unexplained confinement searches for his captor and motive.
Oldboy (2003 film).plot: Dae-su befriends Mi-do and begins a relationship while investigating his imprisonment. Woo-jin staged it as revenge for gossip Dae-su spread about Woo-jin’s incestuous relationship with his sister, who died by suicide. Mi-do is Dae-su’s daughter; hypnosis arranged their relationship. Dae-su removes his tongue to beg for secrecy. Woo-jin kills himself. Dae-su later seeks hypnosis to forget the discovery, with an ambiguous outcome.

Psycho (1960 film).premise: Marion Crane steals money and stops at Norman Bates’s roadside motel.
Psycho (1960 film).plot: Marion is killed while showering, and Norman conceals her body and car. Investigator Arbogast is also murdered. Marion’s sister Lila and lover Sam investigate. Lila discovers the preserved corpse of Norman’s mother; Norman attacks dressed as her. He had killed his mother and her lover and subsequently enacted a murderous mother identity. Norman is detained and Marion’s car recovered.

Saw (2004 film).premise: Adam and doctor Lawrence Gordon awaken chained in a room and face a deadly survival test.
Saw (2004 film).plot: Their captor’s instructions threaten Gordon’s family. Detective Tapp pursues the apparent hostage-taker Zep. Gordon amputates his foot and shoots Adam, then crawls away to get help. Adam survives and kills Zep, learning Zep was also a coerced participant. The apparent corpse in the room is John Kramer, the actual Jigsaw. He rises and locks Adam inside after revealing that Adam’s key was lost down the drain.

The Others (2001 film).premise: Grace protects her light-sensitive children in a darkened house where unexplained visitors appear.
The Others (2001 film).plot: Three servants arrive, and Grace grows convinced that intruders haunt the home. Her husband briefly returns, then leaves. The servants’ graves show that they died decades earlier. During a séance, Grace learns she smothered her children and killed herself. The supposed intruders are living occupants; Grace’s household are ghosts. The living family leaves, while Grace and her children remain.

The Prestige.premise: Rival stage magicians pursue increasingly elaborate illusions and sabotage each other.
The Prestige.plot: Julia’s drowning sparks Angier and Borden’s rivalry. Angier commissions Tesla’s duplicating machine, using copies whose nightly performances end with one drowning. Borden is convicted of Angier’s apparent murder and executed. Borden’s identical twin, previously disguised as Fallon, kills the surviving Angier. The brothers shared one identity and different romances. The surviving brother retrieves his daughter as the theater burns.

Memento.premise: Leonard, unable to form lasting new memories, uses tattoos, photographs and notes to pursue his wife’s attacker.
Memento.plot: Natalie manipulates Leonard into driving away Dodd. Leonard kills Jimmy under Teddy’s guidance. Teddy claims the original attacker was killed earlier, Leonard’s wife survived the assault, and Leonard repeatedly invents new revenge targets. Leonard deliberately destroys evidence and records Teddy’s license number as a clue. His later search therefore leads him to kill Teddy. The narrative’s competing accounts remain unreliable.

Rebecca.premise: An unnamed young woman marries widower Maxim de Winter and struggles with his first wife’s legacy at Manderley.
Rebecca.plot: Mrs Danvers undermines the new wife. Discovery of Rebecca’s submerged body prompts Maxim to admit shooting her and sinking the boat; their admired marriage was a facade. An investigation discovers Rebecca had terminal cancer and could not have been pregnant, undermining a threatened accusation against Maxim. The couple returns to see Manderley burning, following Danvers’s disappearance.

Jane Eyre.premise: An orphan overcomes harsh upbringing and becomes a governess, developing feelings for her employer Rochester.
Jane Eyre.plot: Jane endures the Reeds and Lowood school, where Helen dies. At Thornfield she loves Rochester, but their wedding is stopped by disclosure of his living wife Bertha, confined in the house. Jane leaves, inherits money, finds cousins and rejects St John’s marriage proposal. Bertha later dies in a fire after Rochester attempts rescue and is injured. Jane returns and marries him.

The Great Gatsby.premise: Nick Carraway observes his wealthy neighbor Gatsby and the social world around Daisy and Tom Buchanan.
The Great Gatsby.plot: Gatsby pursues reunion with Daisy, his former love, despite her marriage to Tom. Their affair leads to a confrontation. Driving Gatsby’s car, Daisy fatally strikes Tom’s mistress Myrtle. Gatsby accepts responsibility. Tom directs Myrtle’s husband George toward Gatsby; George kills Gatsby and then himself. Few attend Gatsby’s funeral. Disillusioned Nick returns to the Midwest.

Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde.premise: Lawyer Utterson investigates the troubling connection between respected Jekyll and violent Hyde.
Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde.plot: Hyde tramples a girl and later murders Carew. Jekyll’s seclusion worsens. Lanyon dies after witnessing Hyde transform into Jekyll. Utterson and Poole break into the laboratory and discover Hyde dead. Jekyll’s account explains his serum-created alternate identity, increasingly involuntary transformations, and the failure of replacement ingredients. With the original supply exhausted, Jekyll expects his own identity to disappear permanently.

And Then There Were None.premise: Ten people gather on an isolated island and are accused of responsibility for past deaths.
And Then There Were None.plot: The guests die in a sequence echoing a nursery rhyme, while figurines disappear. Wargrave apparently dies, Armstrong disappears, and the remaining guests suspect each other. Vera kills Lombard and hangs herself. A later confession reveals Wargrave organized the murders, deceived Armstrong into helping stage his death, killed Armstrong and ultimately shot himself to leave a seemingly impossible mystery.

Inception.premise: Cobb steals secrets through shared dreams and is offered a return home for successfully planting an idea.
Inception.plot: The team targets Fischer across a rainy city, Arthur’s hotel and Eames’s fortress. Yusuf drives the van; Arthur remains at his level and improvises an elevator kick after the van falls. Coordinated kicks return the team through the layers. Cobb’s projection of Mal disrupts the plan, and he acknowledges implanting her belief that reality was a dream. Fischer accepts the idea; Cobb rescues Saito, returns home and leaves his spinning top unobserved.

Breaking Bad.premise: A chemistry teacher diagnosed with cancer partners with former student Jesse to make methamphetamine for his family.
Breaking Bad.plot: Across season one, Walt kills Krazy-8, hides his activities from Skyler, declines Elliott and Gretchen’s assistance with treatment, and develops a dangerous arrangement with Tuco. In season two Hank kills Tuco, Saul helps the business and introduces Walt to distributor Gus Fring after Combo dies. Walt misses his daughter’s birth for a delivery and later lets Jane choke. Her grieving father’s air-traffic error causes a collision.

Sintel.premise: A young traveler seeks her lost dragon companion Scales.
Sintel.plot: Sintel rescues the injured young dragon, but another dragon carries him away. Her search leads through a mountain ambush and a shaman’s hut; the spear points toward dragon territory. She finds a cave and attacks an adult dragon, recognizing its wing scar too late: she has killed the grown Scales. Her reflection reveals the years consumed by her quest. She departs grieving, followed by Scales’s offspring.
